name: MonarchEventPopover
title: EventPopover
wrapsNative: Content for MonarchPopover (androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup) or androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet; android.icu.text.DateFormat for the times; MonarchDescriptionList for the details; MonarchBadge for the status; androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow for the actions
summary: The content of a quick view of a calendar event: color swatch, title, subtitle, status badge, date and time in a stated zone, labelled details, a note and actions.
whenToUse: When a person taps an event in a calendar, agenda or booking list and needs its time, place and people without leaving the screen.
whenNotToUse: For the event in a grid or list, use MonarchEventChip. For editing an event, open a full screen or a sheet with a form.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEventPopover(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, subtitle: String? = null, start: Long? = null, end: Long? = null, allDay: Boolean = false, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, status: MonarchEventChipStatus? = null, details: List<MonarchEventPopoverDetail> = emptyList(), note: String? = null, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchEventPopoverLabels = MonarchEventPopoverLabels(), actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchEventPopoverDetail(label: String, value: String, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchEventPopoverLabels(time: String? = null, allDay: String? = null, status: ((MonarchEventChipStatus) -> String)? = null)

options.name: subtitle
options.description: A second line under the title, such as the calendar or the service.

options.name: start
options.description: When the event starts, in epoch milliseconds (UTC); for an all-day event its first day as a UTC midnight. Without it there is no time row.

options.name: end
options.description: When the event ends; for an all-day event its last day, inclusive. An end before the start is ignored.

options.name: allDay
options.description: Shows the day or day range and "All day" instead of times.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's color for the swatch. Unspecified uses the accent role.

options.name: status
options.description: Confirmed, tentative, cancelled or declined, shown as a badge in the success, warning, neutral or danger tone.

options.name: details
options.description: Labelled rows under the time, shown as an inline MonarchDescriptionList. A row's icon is shown before its value.

options.name: note
options.description: A sentence on a subtle fill under the details, such as a cancellation reason.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone the times are shown in, named after the times. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Time", "All day" and the status names (strings_eventpopover.xml).

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons at the bottom, laid out in a wrapping row. The app dismisses the popover or sheet from them.

states.name: spans days
states.description: The start day and time on the first line, the end day, time and zone on the second.

states.name: all day
states.description: The day or "first – last" day range, then "All day".

states.name: confirmed, tentative, cancelled, declined
states.description: A badge with the status name in its tone; cancelled and declined titles are struck through.

states.name: no time
states.description: Without start the time row is left out.

appearance: A small round swatch in the event color or the accent role, the title as a subheading in default text, the subtitle and the times in muted text, the status as a subtle MonarchBadge, details as an inline description list with muted terms, and the note on the subtle background with the control corner radius. Inside MonarchPopover it sits on the raised surface with a shadow. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web EventPopover includes its own Popover and trigger. On Android, as on iOS, this is the content: put it in a MonarchPopover next to the MonarchEventChip that opens it, or in a ModalBottomSheet on a phone; they handle dismissal and focus return. The web's hourCycle option has no counterpart: Android follows the person's 12 or 24 hour setting through the locale's skeleton. Product-specific statuses (the web's custom status node) are not supported; pass labels.status to rename the built-in ones. Dates are epoch milliseconds, not ISO strings; the zone is an IANA id, as on the web. Detail rows always show their label; an icon is shown before the value rather than replacing the label as on the web and iOS, because the rows are a MonarchDescriptionList.
accessibility: The title is a heading; the swatch is decorative.
The status is a badge with its name in words, so it does not rely on color; cancelled and declined titles are also struck through.
The time row is one element read as "Time, Sat, Nov 14, 2026, 9:30 AM – 10:15 AM EST".
Each detail row is one element read as its label and value; detail icons are hidden.
Actions are separate buttons with 48dp targets that wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.
edgeCases: An end before the start is ignored and only the start is shown.
All-day dates are formatted in UTC so a UTC-midnight day does not move with the device zone.
ICU writes a narrow no-break space before AM and PM in recent locale data.
Without start there is no time row, for example for a task without a due time.

examples.title: From an event chip
An all-day event with a note
examples.code:
MonarchEventPopover(
    title = "Team offsite",
    start = 1_794_614_400_000L,
    end = 1_794_700_800_000L,
    allDay = true,
    status = MonarchEventChipStatus.Cancelled,
    note = "Cancelled because of the rail strike.",
)
